lesson_title: Up With Up, or Up With Down? Proportion in One Question
hook_text: Six people paint a wall in 10 days. Four people take... NOT fewer days. Here's the one question that stops that mistake.
clip_script: Here is the only question you need before any proportion problem: when I increase the first thing, does the second thing go UP or go DOWN? Bread. Three loaves cost R51. More loaves, more money — up with up. That is direct proportion: 51 divided by 3 is R17 a loaf, so seven loaves cost R119. Painting. Six people take 10 days. If only four turn up — fewer hands, more days. Up with down. That is indirect proportion: 6 times 10 is 60 person-days, and the wall needs 60 of them no matter who comes. Four people need 60 divided by 4 — 15 days. Ask the question first, and the method chooses itself.
visual_style: A split screen: on the left, loaves and rand both stacking upward in step; on the right, a see-saw with painters on one end and a calendar on the other, tipping as painters are removed and days pile up.
pacing: Pose the question slowly, then two brisk worked examples, and land hard on 'ask first'.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort every proportion problem with one question.
